served.stem: The molecule below is 2-bromo-3-chlorobutane drawn with both stereocenters defined. Assign the (C2, C3) configuration. (Number from the bromine-bearing carbon as C2.)
served.bankWhy: (2R,3R). It is not meso because the two ends carry different halogens (Br vs Cl), so no internal mirror plane. Keyed correct=0 is right; the meso distractors are good traps.

answer.line: Swap H onto the dash or wedge at each center and both read R. The ends differ, so it is (2R, 3R), chiral.

steps: Start with C2. Rank by atomic number: Br (1), then C3, which carries Cl (2), then CH3 (3), then H (4).
At C2, H lies flat and Br sits on the dash. Swap them so H points away. Trace 1 to 2 to 3: counterclockwise, S. Flip once for the swap: R.
C3: Cl (1), C2 with its Br (2), CH3 (3), H (4). Swap H with Cl on the wedge. Trace: clockwise, R. Flip for H toward you, flip for the swap: R.
Meso check. Meso needs matching halves, and one end has Br while the other has Cl. No mirror plane: chiral, not meso.

choices.note: The wedge at C3 holds Cl, not H. Swap them and the two flips cancel, so C3 reads as traced: R.
Both letters reversed is the enantiomer. With Br on one center and Cl on the other, this molecule cannot be meso.
C3 is right, C2 is not. This is C2 traced as drawn, with H still flat. Swap H onto the dash first, then flip once for the swap.
Both centers R, and no mirror plane.
The letters match, but meso needs matching ends. Br and Cl differ, so the molecule is chiral.

student.lockIt: Assign each stereocenter on its own. Meso needs matching groups on both centers and a mirror plane.
student.hook: Every swap flips the letter. Count your flips.
